text: Welcome here. I see you are a newborn; could you describe any specific changes in your skin, breathing, or feeding habits that you've noticed?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. Since there are no immunization records, have you noticed any yellowing of the skin or eyes, or has the baby been having trouble feeding and staying awake? REQUEST TEST: Bilirubin_level

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Cellulitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Rubella Syndrome

The combination of a continuous heart murmur (likely a Patent Ductus Arteriosus), bluish non-blanching macules (Purpura Fulminans), cloudy lenses (Congenital Cataracts), and hearing loss is classic for this condition. The previous suggestion of cellulitis is incorrect given the specific nature of the skin findings and the systemic symptoms.
